findings.title: removeModelRun now permanently deletes run data under the same endpoint/URL/params that used to only unregister it
findings.suggested_fix: This is a deliberate, documented behavior change (README 'Deleting a run deletes it'), but the endpoint name, URL, HTTP method and request body (model_run_id) are all unchanged from the old unregister-only version. Any script or agent written against the old contract that called removeModelRun expecting a safe unregister will now destroy data irrecoverably the first time it authenticates successfully. Consider a distinct response marker (e.g. a 'destructive': true field) or a renamed endpoint (deleteModelRun) for any future breaking change of this kind, and call this one out explicitly in a CHANGELOG/release note beyond the README prose.

findings.title: scanModelRuns and registerModelRun were hard-removed with no compatibility stub, unlike removeModelRun which got an interim informative response
findings.suggested_fix: In commit df59409, removeModelRun was temporarily turned into a JSON 501 ('Removing a run is unavailable...') before later being reimplemented, giving callers a machine-readable signal during the transition. scanModelRuns and registerModelRun were deleted outright in the same commit with no equivalent stub, so any external/agent caller now gets Django's default HTML 404 instead of a JSON error, breaking the API's otherwise-consistent {"error": ...} error shape for these two routes. If external callers are a real concern, add a short-lived JSON 410 Gone stub for both routes pointing callers at createUpload/startUpload/uploadRun instead of removing them outright.

findings.title: getModelRuns dropped the `rescannable` field from every entry with no replacement or version signal
findings.suggested_fix: Base commit's get_model_runs_selectable() returned {value, label, rescannable} for every run; at HEAD it returns only {value, label}. The in-repo frontend never read `rescannable` (confirmed via grep), so this is safe for the shipped client, but it is a subtractive change to a field an external/agent caller could have depended on. No deprecation period, no version bump, and not called out in README. If external consumers of getModelRuns are a real concern, document the removal in a changelog; otherwise this is low-risk given the single first-party consumer.

findings.title: getModelRuns' id/value field changed format from a stable UUID to a free-form run name for any run created going forward
findings.suggested_fix: Before this branch, `id` in getModelRuns/model_run_id was always a Django UUIDField value. Now (utils.py _entry_from_manifest, line ~130, reading manifest.distill's `"id": run_id or os.path.basename(run_path)`) a freshly-created or freshly-uploaded run's id is its directory/run name, which need not be a UUID at all. Backward compatibility for existing shared '?model_run_id=' links is handled via `legacy_uuids` in _get_model_run_path_by_id, which is good, but any external caller that validates model_run_id as a UUID (regex, DB column type, etc.) will start rejecting valid ids for every newly created run. Document that model_run_id is now an opaque string rather than a UUID, if external callers are expected to consume this field.

findings.title: removeModelRun's response codes for unauthenticated/unauthorized callers changed from 200 to 401/403
findings.suggested_fix: Intentional and well-documented security fix (README: 'Changing a run requires signing in') paired with a genuinely destructive new default behavior, so the narrowing is justified. Flagging only because any pre-existing automation that called removeModelRun anonymously and treated a 200 as success will now see 401, and any caller that has a session but lacks the new delete_model_runs permission will see 403 for the first time. No action needed beyond ensuring this is called out in release notes for the hosted/open-portal deployments most likely to have existing anonymous automation.

residual_risks: No dedicated API reference (endpoint list, request/response schemas) exists anywhere in the repo; README documents CLI/workflow changes well but not the JS/HTTP API surface, so future contract changes to createUpload/startUpload/uploadRun/uploadStatus have nothing to be checked against besides app.test.js.

uploadStatus returns whatever JSON keys the ingest_archive subprocess happened to write (job, updated, state, stage, message, run) plus a synthesized `terminal`; this is internally consistent across all write_status call sites today, but there is no schema enforcement, so a future call site that omits `run` or `message` would silently degrade the client's polling UI rather than fail loudly.

There is no API versioning mechanism in this app at all (no /v1/ prefix, no version header, no App.version bump visible in this diff), so any future breaking change to these Tethys controller endpoints will have the same hard-cutover characteristics observed here.
testing_gaps: No Python-level tests exist for controllers.py (tethysapp/ngiab/tests/ only contains a stale __pycache__, no test_*.py), so the new permission gating (401 vs 403 vs 200), the destructive removeModelRun path, and the createUpload/startUpload/uploadRun/uploadStatus flow are only exercised (if at all) through frontend JS tests against a mocked fetch, not against the real Django views.

app.test.js pins the client-side surface (createUpload, startUpload, uploadRunUrl, uploadStatus, removeModelRun) and confirms scanModelRuns/registerModelRun are gone from appAPI, but there is no test anywhere asserting the actual HTTP status codes (401/403/404/409) the server returns for these endpoints under different auth states.
